question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 22\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 22\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=22\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-16 \\ {x}_{2} &=8\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=8$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1}-(8) &=-9 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=8$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=22 \\ 2(-1)+3(8) &=22 \\ 22 &=22\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=8$, which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+8{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-1)+(8)=7.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=4 \\ {x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=4$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=4$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=4 \\ -{x}_{1}+(4) &=4 \\ -{x}_{1} &=0 \\ {x}_{1} &=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=0$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -(0)+2(4) &=7 \\ 8 &=7\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=2$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=3 \\ (2)-{x}_{2} &=3 \\ -{x}_{2} &=1 \\ {x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$, which means

$$
2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(2)+(-1)=1.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ -15 \\ 23\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=23\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-1) &=-15 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-18 \\ {x}_{1} &=9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=9$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=23 \\ 3(9)+5(-1) &=23 \\ 22 &=23\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -30\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -30\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -30\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -30\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-13 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=17 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-30\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-9\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-9$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=17 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-9) &=17 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-10 \\ {x}_{1} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=-9$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-30 \\ 3(5)+5(-9) &=-30 \\ -30 &=-30\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=-9$, which means

$$
5{a}_{1}-9{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(5)+(-9)=-4.
$$
